final_proof:
Let \(\psi=\phi^{-1}:A_2\to A_1\). Since \(\phi\) is bijective, its inverse \(\psi\) exists and is itself bijective. In particular, the two correctly typed inverse identities are \(\psi\circ\phi=\operatorname{id}_{A_1}\) and \(\phi\circ\psi=\operatorname{id}_{A_2}\).

It remains to prove that \(\psi\) preserves arbitrary joins and arbitrary meets. Let \(S\subseteq A_2\) be arbitrary, and put \(T=\psi[S]=\{\psi(s):s\in S\}\subseteq A_1\). We have \(\phi[T]=S\). Indeed, if \(s\in S\), then \(s=\phi(\psi(s))\in\phi[T]\); conversely, if \(y\in\phi[T]\), then \(y=\phi(\psi(s))=s\) for some \(s\in S\), and hence \(y\in S\).

Because \(\phi\) is a complete lattice homomorphism, it preserves the join of every subset of \(A_1\). Therefore
\[
\phi\!\left(\bigvee_{L_1}T\right)=\bigvee_{L_2}\phi[T]=\bigvee_{L_2}S.
\]
Applying \(\psi\) to both sides and using \(\psi\circ\phi=\operatorname{id}_{A_1}\), we obtain
\[
\psi\!\left(\bigvee_{L_2}S\right)=\bigvee_{L_1}T=\bigvee_{L_1}\psi[S].
\]
Thus \(\psi\) preserves arbitrary joins.

Similarly, preservation by \(\phi\) of the meet of every subset gives
\[
\phi\!\left(\bigwedge_{L_1}T\right)=\bigwedge_{L_2}\phi[T]=\bigwedge_{L_2}S.
\]
Applying \(\psi\) again yields
\[
\psi\!\left(\bigwedge_{L_2}S\right)=\bigwedge_{L_1}T=\bigwedge_{L_1}\psi[S].
\]
Thus \(\psi\) preserves arbitrary meets. The argument also covers \(S=\varnothing\), because completeness supplies the empty join and empty meet and a complete lattice homomorphism preserves them as part of preserving all joins and meets. Consequently \(\phi^{-1}=\psi:L_2\to L_1\) is a bijective complete lattice homomorphism.
